context.rule: Greeting: name or 你 / 您 / 你们 + 好

why: 您 is the polite form of 你, used for a teacher. 您好 is a respectful greeting.

not.不: 不 is a negative word; 老师，不好 would mean 'not good'.
not.吗: 吗 turns a statement into a question; it is not a greeting word.
not.没: 没 negates 有 or past actions; it does not make a greeting.

context.rule: Greeting: name or 你 / 您 / 你们 + 好

why: 你们 is the plural of 你, so it fits a group. 你们好 means hello to several people.

not.您: 您 is polite for one person, not a group.
not.好: 好 follows a person word; 好好 is not a greeting here.
not.不: 不 means no/not; it cannot start a greeting.

context.rule: Greeting: name or 你 / 您 / 你们 + 好

why: After 对不起 (sorry), the usual reply is 没关系, meaning 'it doesn't matter'.

not.你好: 你好 is a hello, not a reply to an apology.
not.你们: 你们 means 'you (plural)', not a reply.
not.您好: 您好 is a polite hello, not a reply to sorry.

why: 不客气 means 'you're welcome'. 不 goes before the phrase 客气 to say 'don't be polite'.

not.没: 没 is used with 有 or past actions; 没客气 is not the set phrase.
not.很: 很客气 means 'very polite', not 'you're welcome'.
not.吗: 吗 makes questions; B is giving a reply.

why: 不 goes before 是 to make 'am not'. 我不是老师 means I am not a teacher.

not.吗: 吗 goes at the end of a question, not before 是.
not.很: 很 goes before adjectives, not before 是.
not.的: 的 joins a word to a noun; it does not make "not".

why: 再见 means goodbye and is a natural way to end after 谢谢 and 不客气.

not.对不起: 对不起 is for saying sorry; nothing here needs an apology.
not.没关系: 没关系 answers an apology, not thanks.
not.谢谢: B already replied to thanks; saying 谢谢 again does not close the talk.

context.rule: A 是 B: A is B

why: 是 links two nouns: 我是学生 means 'I am a student'.

not.叫: 叫 means 'be called' and needs a name after it.
not.有: 有 means 'have'; it does not say what someone is.
not.很: 很 goes with adjectives, not before a noun like 学生.

context.rule: A 是 B: A is B

why: 不 comes before 是, so 她不是老师 means 'she is not a teacher'.

not.叫: 叫 needs a name; 老师 is a job, not a name.
not.吗: 吗 only comes at the end of a question.
not.好: 好 is an adjective; 她不好老师 makes no sense.

why: Adding 吗 to the end of a statement makes it a yes/no question: 你是中国人吗？

not.呢: 呢 asks 'and you?' after a topic, not a yes/no question here.
not.的: 的 links words; it does not make a question.
not.什么: 什么 replaces the missing word; here nothing is missing.

why: The statement 你是老师 becomes a yes/no question with 吗 at the end.

not.什么: 什么 asks "what", but 老师 is already said; this is a yes/no question.
not.谁: 谁 asks "who", but the person word 老师 is already there.
not.哪: 哪 needs a noun after it, like 哪国.

context.rule: 什么 asks “what”, in the place of the answer

why: 什么 takes the place of the answer. 名字 is a thing to ask about, so 什么名字 means 'what name'.

not.吗: 吗 comes at the end of a sentence, not before 名字.
not.谁: 谁 asks about a person, not a name.
not.哪: 哪 means 'which' and is used with a measure word or 国.

context.rule: 什么 asks “what”, in the place of the answer

why: 这是 asks about a thing, so 什么 ('what') fits: 这是什么？

not.吗: 这是吗 is missing what "this" is; 吗 needs a full statement.
not.哪: 哪 means 'which' and needs a noun after it.
not.几: 几 asks about small numbers, not what a thing is.

context.rule: 谁 = who, 哪 + 国 = which country

why: 谁 asks 'who'. It stands where the person's name would be.

not.吗: 吗 would ask yes/no and cannot replace the person word.
not.哪: 哪 asks 'which' and needs a noun, like 哪国.
not.几: 几 asks about numbers, not a person.

context.rule: 谁 = who, 哪 + 国 = which country

why: 哪 + 国 + 人 asks which country someone is from: 哪国人.

not.谁: 谁 asks about a person, not a country.
not.什么: 什么国人 is not the normal way to ask this.
not.几: 几 asks for a small number, not a place.

why: 的 joins owner and thing: 我的老师 means 'my teacher'.

not.是: 是 is a verb; 她是我是老师 would repeat the verb.
not.呢: 呢 asks 'and you?', not showing ownership.

why: 谁的书 means 'whose book'. 的 shows who owns the book.

not.吗: 吗 ends a yes/no question; it cannot sit before 书.
not.是: 是 is a verb; 这是谁是书 is wrong.
not.呢: 呢 ends a short question; it does not link owner and thing.

why: 呢 gives a short question back: 你呢？ means 'and you?' after 我是学生.

not.吗: 吗 needs a full statement before it; 你吗 is not a question.
not.的: 的 needs a noun after it.
not.谁: 谁 means 'who'; 你谁 is not a sentence.

why: 他呢？ asks 'and what about him?' after the speaker says 我是中国人.

not.的: 的 needs a noun after it.
not.是: 他是 would need something after it.
not.什么: 他什么 does not mean 'and him?'.

context.rule: 几 asks small numbers; 多大 asks age
context.en: How many people are in your family?

why: 几 asks about small numbers you can count, like people in a family.

not.多: 多 needs an adjective after it (多大); 多口人 is not Chinese.

context.rule: 几 asks small numbers; 多大 asks age
context.en: How old are you this year?

why: 多大 asks about age: 多 + the adjective 大. 你今年多大了？

not.几: 几 works for young kids (几岁), but 几大 is not a phrase.
not.很: 很大 says 'very big'; it is not a question.
not.太: 太大了 says 'too big'; it is not a question.

context.rule: …了 at the end: a new situation

why: 了 at the end shows a new situation: she has now reached five years old.

not.吗: 吗 would turn it into a question; the English is a statement.
not.的: 的 does not end a statement about age.
not.呢: 呢 asks 'and what about…?'; this is a plain statement.

why: 二十 means 'two tens' = 20. Number + 十 gives tens: 二十, 三十.

not.二二: 二二 is not a number word in Chinese.
not.十十: 十十 is not a number word in Chinese.

why: Teens use 十 first and then the digit: 十 + 三 = 十三, thirteen.

not.一三: Chinese does not say 13 digit by digit like 一三.
not.三一: 三一 is not a number word for 13 or 31.

why: 会 means 'can' for a learned skill. Speaking Chinese is learned, so 我会说汉语.

not.是: 是 links nouns; it cannot go before the verb 说 here.
not.在: 我在说汉语 means "I am speaking Chinese", not "I can".
not.有: 有 means 'have'; it does not mean 'can' here.

why: 会 asks if you have learned a skill: writing characters. 你会写汉字吗？

not.是: 是 links nouns, not a verb like 写.
not.叫: 叫 means 'be called'; it does not go before 写.
not.的: 的 links nouns and cannot be a verb helper here.

context.rule: Adjectives normally take 很: 很好, 很好吃

why: In a plain sentence with an adjective, 很 usually goes before it: 很好吃.

not.是: 是 does not go before an adjective in this plain statement.
not.会: 会 is for skills, not to describe food.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question; the English is a statement.

context.rule: 怎么 asks how to do something
context.en: How do you read this character?

why: 怎么 + verb asks how to do something. 怎么读 means 'how to read'.

not.什么: 什么读 is not the way to ask 'how'; 什么 asks 'what'.

context.rule: 怎么 asks how to do something

why: 怎么说 asks how to say it. 怎么 comes before the verb 说.

not.什么: 什么 asks "what"; it does not go before 说 to ask "how".
not.哪: 哪 means 'which' and needs a noun.
not.谁: 谁说 asks "who says it", not how to say it.

context.rule: year → month 月 → day 号 → 星期

why: Dates end with 号 for the day: 九月一号 is September 1st.

not.月: 月 is the month; 九月 is already said.
not.年: 年 is the year, not the day.
not.点: 点 is for clock time like 八点.

context.rule: year → month 月 → day 号 → 星期

why: 星期几 asks which day of the week. 几 is used for small numbers like 1 to 7.

not.什么: 星期什么 is not used to ask the weekday.
not.多少: 多少 is for bigger numbers; the week has only seven days.

context.en: I'm going to school to read.

why: 去 + place + verb says going somewhere to do something: 去学校看书.

not.是: 是 does not mean going somewhere.
not.有: 有 means 'have'; it does not show movement.

context.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the shop to buy a cup.

why: 买 means 'buy'. The sentence says I go to the shop to buy a cup: 去商店买杯子.

not.吃: 吃 means 'eat'; you do not eat a cup.
not.喝: 喝 means 'drink'; you drink from a cup, not the cup itself.
not.看: 看 means "look"; the English says buy a cup.

context.rule: 想: want to, would like to

why: 想 goes before a verb to say 'would like to': 我想喝茶.

not.是: 是 does not go before a verb like 喝.
not.在: 在 + verb means 'is doing', not 'would like'.
not.的: 的 links nouns, so it cannot go here.

context.rule: 想: want to, would like to
context.en: What do you want to do this afternoon?

why: 想 asks what you want to do. 你想做什么？ means 'what do you want to do?'

not.是: 是 does not go before a verb like 做.
not.在: 在 + verb means 'is doing'; the question is about wishes.

context.rule: 多少 asks numbers (often over 10) and prices

why: 多少 asks numbers, often large ones, and prices. 多少钱 means 'how much money'.

not.几: 几 is for small numbers; prices use 多少钱.
not.怎么: 怎么 asks 'how', not an amount.

context.en: I want to buy a cup.

why: Before a noun, a number needs a measure word. 个 is the common one for 杯子.

not.块: 块 counts money or pieces; here a cup needs 个.

why: 块 is the spoken word for yuan. 十八块钱 means 18 yuan.

not.个: 个 counts things; here it is a price.

context.en: The kitten is under the chair.

why: 在 shows where something is: 在椅子下面 means 'under the chair'.

not.是: 是 links nouns; it does not show location with 下面 here.
not.有: 有 means 'have'; the cat is at a place.
not.去: 去 means 'go'; the cat is already there.

why: 在 + place + verb says where someone does something: 在哪儿工作.

not.是: 是 does not go before a place word with a verb here.
not.去: 去哪儿 asks where to go, but the English asks where he works.

why: 哪儿 means 'where'. 在哪儿 asks where the book is.

not.什么: 什么 means 'what'; the question is about place.

context.en: There's a computer on the desk.

why: Place + 有 + thing says what is there: 桌子上有一个电脑.

not.在: 在 puts the thing first (电脑在桌子上), not this order.
not.是: 是 would be 桌子上是…, but 有 is the normal word for 'there is'.

why: 有 + noun asks whether someone or something is there: 这儿有人吗？

not.在: 在 puts the person first (人在这儿); 这儿在人 is wrong.
not.是: 这儿是人吗 asks if 'this place is a person'.
not.的: 的 links nouns and cannot ask if someone is there.

why: 能 before a verb asks or says permission: 我能坐这儿吗？

not.有: 有 means 'have'; 我有坐 is wrong.
not.是: 是 does not go before a verb like 坐.

context.en: There are three books on the desk.

why: Books use the measure word 本. Say 三本书 for three books.

not.个: 个 is common, but books take 本.

context.rule: Time goes before the verb: 我五点回家

why: Clock time uses 点: 八点十分 means 8:10.

not.号: 号 is for the day of the month.

context.rule: Time goes before the verb: 我五点回家

why: 吃 means 'eat'. At noon we eat a meal: 吃饭.

not.喝: 喝 is for drinks; 饭 is food.
not.看: 看 means 'look' and does not go with 饭.
not.买: 买饭 means 'buy a meal', not eat.

why: 什么时候 asks 'when'. It goes before the verb: 你什么时候回家？

not.怎么: 怎么回家 asks 'how', not when.

context.en: We're going to see a movie at three.

why: 看电影 means 'see a movie'. 看 is the verb used with 电影.

not.读: 读 means to read aloud or study; 读电影 is not used.
not.买: 买 means 'buy'; the English says 'see a movie'.

why: 怎么样 asks how something is. 天气怎么样？ means 'how's the weather?'

not.什么: 什么 asks "what thing"; to ask "how is it", use 怎么样.

context.rule: 太 + adjective + 了: too / so …

why: 太 + adjective + 了 means 'too / so …'. 太热了 says it is very hot.

not.很: For "so hot!" with 了, use 太热了; 很热 usually has no 了.
not.不: 不热了 means "not hot any more", the opposite of the English.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and does not fit 热了 here.

context.rule: 会 a skill; 能 able or allowed
context.en: It will rain tomorrow; we can't go.

why: 不能 means 'cannot'. Rain makes going impossible: 不能去.

not.是: 是 does not go before 去 here.
not.有: 不有 is wrong; 有 is negated with 没.
not.的: 的 links nouns and cannot go here.

context.rule: 在 + verb + 呢: doing it right now
context.en: He is learning to cook Chinese food.

why: 在 + verb + 呢 says someone is doing it now: 在学做中国菜呢.

not.是: 是 does not show an action in progress.
not.去: 他去学 means "he goes to learn"; 在…呢 says he is learning now.

context.rule: 在 + verb + 呢: doing it right now

why: 呢 at the end with 在 shows an action in progress: 我在看电视呢.

not.吗: 吗 would make it a question.
not.吧: 吧 suggests 'let's…'; this is a statement.
not.的: 的 does not end a progress sentence.

why: 吧 at the end makes a suggestion: 我们去吃饭吧 means 'let's go eat'.

not.吗: 吗 asks yes/no; it is not a suggestion.
not.呢: 呢 does not make a suggestion; the English says "let's".
not.的: 的 does not make a suggestion.

why: 给 + person + verb means doing something to or for a person: 给你打电话.

not.在: 在 shows where; it does not link a person to calling.
not.和: 和你打电话 means 'with you', not 'to you'.
not.是: 是 does not link a person to an action.

context.en: She bought quite a few clothes.

why: 了 after a verb shows the action is done. 买了 means 'bought'.

not.的: 的 does not show a finished action.
not.吗: 吗 would make it a question.
not.呢: 呢 goes at the end of a sentence, not right after 买.

context.rule: 没 makes a past action negative (no 了)

why: 没 is used to negate a past action, with no 了: 我没买衣服.

not.不: 不买 usually refers to habit or future, not a past action.
not.了: 了 would show done; the English says 'didn't'.

why: 都 means 'all' and goes before the verb: 我们都是学生.

not.很: 很 goes before adjectives, not before 是.
not.太: 太 goes with adjectives and ends with 了.
not.也: 我们也是学生 is fine, but 也 means "also"; the English says "all".

why: 都 sits before 很 and means 'all'. All the clothes are pretty.

not.太: 太 cannot go before 很; you would say 太漂亮了.
not.了: 了 does not go between 衣服 and 很.
not.的: 的 links nouns and cannot go here.

context.rule: 是 … 的 stresses when / how / where something happened

why: 是…的 stresses how something happened. 坐飞机 is the method, so 的 closes the pattern.

not.了: 了 does not close a 是…的 sentence.
not.呢: 呢 does not close a 是…的 pattern.

context.rule: 是 … 的 stresses when / how / where something happened
context.en: When did you come to Beijing?

why: 是…的 stresses when something happened. 是 goes before the time, 什么时候, and 的 comes at the end.

not.在: 在 does not start a 是…的 pattern.

context.rule: 坐 飞机 / 出租车: travelling by …
context.en: Let's take a taxi to the restaurant.

why: 坐 is the verb for riding in a vehicle: 坐出租车 means 'take a taxi'.

not.开: 开 means "drive"; the English says take a taxi as a passenger.
not.在: 在出租车上 means "in the taxi"; "take a taxi" uses 坐.
not.去: 去 needs a place, so 去出租车 is wrong; 去饭店 comes later.
